Hi Michael,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our onboarding security review and SIG intake, we need a focused bundle of artifacts related to your KMS/HSM controls for the tenant that will host our data. Specifically we're after:

- A snapshot of the KMS access matrix for our tenant (operator roles, last operator action timestamps).
- Evidence that keys used for storage transit (SSE-KMS) are wrapped and that KEKs are not exportable from HSM.
- A short runbook or statement describing your key rotation cadence, trigger conditions, and escrow/backup process.
- Any attestation that HSM operator separation of duties is enforced (outright examples or redacted logs are fine).

Our compliance deadline is next Friday, 2028-07-06. Can you confirm if you can provide this bundle by 2028-06-30 EOD PT? If you need approvals for anything, please call me — Alex Morris (Security Eng) — or reply here.

Thanks,
Alex Morris
Senior InfoSec Engineer
Hightower Finance

Alex —

Appreciate the clear list. We can deliver the bundle by 2028-06-30 EOD PT. Attached are an initial redacted KMS access matrix and the current key rotation runbook (we've redacted operator usernames per our privacy policy).

A few quick notes to set expectations:
- The KMS access matrix includes role mappings (HSM Operator, Crypto Admin, Audit), last-action timestamps, and the last key ceremony ID. We will provide a separate HSM operator separation summary PDF after internal sign-off.
- Our KEKs are rooted in FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSMs from our provider. KEKs are non-exportable; we can provide attestation metadata and the HSM vendor quote for the sealing policy.
- Rotation cadence: default quarterly for tenant master keys, with emergency rotations triggered by CVE-class incidents or suspected compromise. The runbook contains the explicit steps for wrap/unwrap and re-encryption.

I'm looping in Irene (Compliance) and Ben (Crypto Ops) to finalize the HSM separation artifact and to add a short transport-affirmation paragraph about envelope-wrapping and transit TLS/SSE-KMS logging.

Best,
Michael Grant

Alex —

Attached are the HSM operator separation summary and a short sample of the SSE-KMS call flow for your review. Highlights:

- HSMs: vendor 'SecureHSM' model SH-700, FIPS 140-2 Level 3. KEKs are configured with non-exportable attributes; seal/unseal operations are delegated to the HSM cluster control plane.
- Key rotation: tenant master keys rotate quarterly by default; the runbook shows the canary step that rewraps object keys with the new KEK and validates signature checks.
- Transport affirmation: all intra-service communication uses mTLS + TLS1.3; envelope-wrapping metadata (wrapped_key_id, wrapping_algorithm, hsm_key_slot) is recorded in the audit trail. The included log sample shows a typical SSE-KMS Encrypt/Decrypt call sequence (ARNs redacted).

Next steps: if you want the unredacted log set for an evidence review under NDA, we can coordinate a secure SFTP transfer (or provide time-limited access to an audit viewer). Please tell us your preferred transfer method.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Cryptography Engineer
Redwood Inference
